data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 reduces resilience to implementation heterogeneity (different languages/OSs preventing a single exploit from causing correlated crash), but its causal mechanism conflates vulnerability heterogeneity with independence of the failure-triggering set. The problem asks to distinguish truly independent failures from merely-appearing-uncorrelated failures with a shared cause. Implementation heterogeneity blocks only exploits specific to a language/OS; it provides no causal mechanism for non-implementation shared causes such as a common data schema, common protocol semantics, common upstream dependency, or a common logical/architectural flaw in the service itself—which is exactly the second countercondition SRC_002 lists. Under those causes, implementation-diverse services can fail concurrently via the same logical path, so heterogeneity yields apparent-but-not-true independence. The mechanism therefore does not establish the independence it claims; it identifies only one narrow channel (exploit portability) and ignores shared-cause channels that heterogeneous implementations do not decouple.
